title: Async/await in one screen
rememberThis: async/await frees the thread during I/O; it does not make CPU work cheaper.
Return Task or ValueTask. Use async void only for event handlers.
Pass CancellationToken through queue and HTTP consumers; cancellation is cooperative.
Never .Result or .Wait() in libraries — UI deadlock or pool starvation.
TaskCompletionSource bridges callback APIs; use TrySet when timeout races success.
bullets: Sequential await is still sequential wall-clock time; start independent work, then await Task.WhenAll.
The compiler rewrites async methods into IAsyncStateMachine that resumes on completion.
ValueTask avoids a Task allocation on the hot synchronous-success path; do not await a ValueTask twice.
await foreach streams pages from IAsyncEnumerable without buffering the whole result.
ConfigureAwait(false) in shared libraries; ASP.NET Core has no SynchronizationContext.
Deadlock stack: Task.Wait/Result + SynchronizationContext.Send on the same thread.
